capture.final_message:
For the first conjunct, apply the rectangular argument principle to \(f\). The hypotheses ensure that \(f'/f\) is meromorphic, its divisor has finite support in the rectangle, and no zero or pole lies on the boundary. Its residue at \(p\) is the meromorphic order of \(f\) at \(p\), so the normalized boundary integral is the finite sum of the divisor.

For the equivalence, it is simplest to prove both statements independently:

- Obtain the logarithmic zeta bound from a truncated Dirichlet/Euler–Maclaurin representation with truncation length \(N\asymp |t|\). In the region
  \[
  \sigma\ge 1-\frac{A}{\log |t|},
  \]
  one has \(n^{1-\sigma}\le e^A\) for \(n\le N\), making the main sum \(O(\log |t|)\); the pole and remainder terms are uniformly controlled. Choose any sufficiently small \(A\le \tfrac12\).

- For fixed \(T\), use the known nonvanishing of \(\zeta\) on \(\Re s\ge1\), together with absolute convergence sufficiently far right and discreteness of zeros. The zeros with \(|\Im s|\le T\) that could approach the line \(\Re s=1\) are thereby confined to a compact set and form a finite set. Choose \(\sigma<1\) strictly larger than all their real parts. Then \(\zeta(\sigma'+it)\ne0\) whenever \(|t|\le T\) and \(\sigma'\ge\sigma\).

Package these two unconditional conclusions into the `Iff`; the essential input for the second direction is nonvanishing on the line \(\Re s=1\).
